laws.rule: Seoul has declared many outdoor public places smoke-free, including bus stops and the area within 10 metres of every subway station exit (from 1 May 2016). The city's own page lists the 10 metre zone; it is a dated 2016 notice, so the current list of sites isn't confirmed here.
laws.penalty_signal: Seoul's 2016 notice gives a fine of 100,000 won for smoking inside a subway-exit zone. Not converted to AUD (no dated rate held).

laws.rule: Seoul Metropolitan Government can designate outdoor places as smoke-free under the National Health Promotion Act. The ordinance lists the kinds of place it can cover: city parks, riverside walking paths, bus stops and taxi stands, the area within 10 metres of subway station exits, and the area within 10 metres of the swimming pools and water-play areas in Han River parks. The exact designated sites are set by notice and marked by signs, so follow the signs. The ordinance counts holding a lit cigarette as smoking. It does not set the fine itself; Seoul's 2016 notice already on this record gives KRW 100,000.
laws.penalty_signal: Fine is not in the ordinance (see the notice already listed).

laws.rule: Seoul's Han River parks ordinance bans these acts inside the parks: camping or cooking outside designated places; not collecting a pet's droppings; not keeping a dog on a lead; leaving waste, including cigarette butts and chewing gum, outside designated places; not taking away your own picnic rubbish; fishing where it is banned; picking flowers or fruit; harming trees or animals; parking outside designated places; and using wheeled motor devices off the roadway, apart from the exceptions the ordinance lists (for example e-bikes and e-scooters on the bike paths).
laws.penalty_signal: Fines are set in Annex 3 of the ordinance, which could not be read from the text; the amounts are not confirmed here.

laws.rule: The same ordinance bans making severe noise or smells, or getting drunk and disturbing others, in the Han River parks. It does not ban drinking in the parks.
laws.penalty_signal: Fines are set in Annex 3 of the ordinance; amounts not confirmed here.

layers.authority: Bukhansan National Park Office (Korea National Park Service); the trail runs between Seoul (Gangbuk-gu, Dobong-gu) and Yangju in Gyeonggi
layers.process: Uiryeong-gil, a Bukhansan trail that was long restricted, opens to everyone without a reservation on weekdays from April 2026. On weekends and public holidays a prior reservation is still needed. Residents of Gangbuk-gu, Dobong-gu and Yangju-si can walk it after a one-time registration on site. This comes from a news report of the park office's 27 March 2026 announcement; the park service's own page was not read. The quota and booking steps were not given.

sources.title: Uiryeong-gil opens fully on weekdays from April (news report)
